p: Advanced audio tools for Unreal Engine — MetaSound playback, acoustic processing, and Blueprint utilities.
Welcome to the AudioPhysx documentation. This draft site is being prepared for the Fab release and is not yet an assurance that every feature has completed packaged-game validation.

This example uses AP: Sequence Wave Player to play multiple recordings one after another.
Create a MetaSound Source with a mono output.
Add AP: Sequence Wave Player from AudioPhysx → Playback.
Expand the Sequence Waves group and connect a Wave Asset to each Wave slot.
Connect the MetaSound On Play trigger to the node's Play input.
Connect Out Mono to the MetaSound audio output.
Connect On Finished to the MetaSound Source's completion trigger, if you want the source to finish automatically.
Preview playback with Loop Sequence disabled, then try enabling it.
Each playable wave should finish before the next starts. Stop stops the sequence. The On Finished trigger indicates the completed sequence rather than the end of each individual wave.

Plays a selected introduction, followed by repeated middle sounds, followed by a selected ending when firing stops. The middle section supports either completion-based playback or an RPM-driven shot cadence.
At 0, preserve sequential middle playback; positive values schedule overlapping middle-shot starts.
Choose whether to move promptly into the ending or finish outstanding playback first.
Request transition into the ending section.
Sequence complete after release and remaining audio.

Supply one or more starting recordings, several short main-shot variations, and a set of release recordings. For a 600 RPM cadence, the scheduled interval is 60 / 600 = 0.1 s (100 ms). This does not require each middle recording to last 100 ms; shots may overlap.
RPM = 0 uses the older completion-driven behaviour and also suits machinery.
Stop Firing is a release request, not necessarily an immediate silence command.
The number of simultaneously active shots is bounded by the player implementation.
On Finished should not be treated as proof of an external gameplay action completing.

The flyby path helpers are designed to work from path and speed data supplied by the game, without requiring Chaos rigid-body simulation. Other physics-related features may use engine queries depending on the setup.

l: Can Sound Cues use these MetaSound nodes?
p: No. The MetaSound nodes live inside MetaSound graphs. Dedicated Sound Cue QoL nodes are planned separately and are not yet part of this source version.

l: Are future Unreal Engine versions guaranteed?
p: No. Native code plugins must be tested and submitted for the specific engine versions advertised.

l: Plugin fails to compile after replacing source
p: Verify the editor was closed and Live Coding is disabled.
Make sure the old source folder was replaced, not merged; stale .cpp files can cause duplicate registrations or symbols.
If generated-header errors appear following reflection declaration changes, delete generated plugin/project Intermediate outputs and rebuild cleanly.
Check the exact first compiler error, not only the final UnrealBuildTool failure message.
Check AudioPhysx is enabled and the correct editor target built successfully.
Search using the full name, such as AP: Start Loop End Player.
Restart the editor when dynamic-interface configuration changes.

l: Sequence plays silence or ends unexpectedly
p: Verify the Wave Asset inputs are assigned, cooked and playable in the target project.
Test simple mono PCM assets first, then compressed/streamed formats.
Check the player Stop/Stop Firing control flow and that the MetaSound itself is not stopped prematurely.
